rows.citation: Gerkin R, Omar C (scidash) (2011). SciUnit: A Python framework for test-driven validation of scientific models. GitHub repository scidash/sciunit; PyPI sciunit 0.2.8.
rows.controlled_mutations: no: validates models against observational data; no seeded model faults or mutant generation found in README or package layout.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no: domain-agnostic; stimulation protocols are left to domain libraries such as NeuronUnit.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no: provides generic scores and comparators; no electrophysiology feature definitions in the core package.
rows.protocol_optimization: no: supports test suites and score matrices, but no selection or minimisation of test sets.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: no discovery/held-out split concept for tests or models.
rows.ai_transformations: no: no AI-assisted model editing or evaluation.
rows.software: SciUnit https://github.com/scidash/sciunit (MIT per GitHub API, README and PyPI; PyPI sciunit 0.2.8 uploaded 2024-01-03; last push 2023-12-26)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Reusable test/score scaffolding only. NeuroSem would add neuron-specific reference-vs-transformed comparison, refinement-calibrated tolerances, seeded single-fault mutants, greedy protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repos/scidash/sciunit (created 2011-12-05, MIT); raw README.md (contributors, concept); PyPI JSON API sciunit (author Rick Gerkin, version, license, upload date); GitHub contents API for package layout.
rows.found_via: GitHub REST API api.github.com/repos/scidash/sciunit (license MIT) | GitHub REST API repos/scidash/sciunit (MIT) and PyPI JSON API https://pypi.org/pypi/sciunit/json (MIT)

rows.citation: Gerkin R (scidash) (2012). NeuronUnit: A package for data-driven validation of neuron and ion channel models using SciUnit. GitHub repository scidash/neuronunit; PyPI neuronunit 0.1.8.2.
rows.model_type: single-neuron and ion-channel models, including NeuroML channel files and Open Source Brain models via wrappers
rows.controlled_mutations: no: tests models against experimental data (e.g. NeuroElectro summaries); no seeded single-fault mutants found.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes: test modules include rheobase search, injected square-current tests, passive, waveform and dynamics tests.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: resting potential, spike width, rheobase and related features scored (e.g. Z-scores) against observations.
rows.protocol_optimization: no: has an optimization subpackage (e.g. neuronunit_to_bpo) apparently for model fitting; not read in detail; no protocol-set selection found.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: no held-out models or held-out fault families for evaluating a test battery.
rows.software: NeuronUnit https://github.com/scidash/neuronunit (GitHub API: no license detected; setup.py and PyPI declare MIT; last push 2021-07-18; PyPI neuronunit 0.1.8.2 from 2016)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest reusable neuron test library, but it measures agreement with data. NeuroSem targets behavioural drift versus a reference model, calibrates tolerances numerically, uses controlled mutants and selects a compact battery evaluated on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repos/scidash/neuronunit (created 2012-11-01, license null); raw README.md; GitHub contents API for neuronunit/, tests/, optimization/; raw tests/fi.py (RheobaseTest) and setup.py (license MIT); PyPI JSON API neuronunit.
rows.found_via: WebSearch NeuronUnit; GitHub REST API api.github.com/repos/scidash/neuronunit (no SPDX license reported by API)

rows.citation: Mandge D, Tuncel A, Jaquier A, et al. (2026). eFEL: electrophysiology feature extraction library. Bioinformatics 42(6), btag328.
rows.model_type: voltage traces from experimental recordings and simulated neuron models (feature-extraction tool, model-agnostic)
rows.controlled_mutations: no: library paper; no seeded model faults or mutation analysis in abstract or full text.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial: accepts traces from any stimulus with user-set stimulus windows; paper does not design or compare stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: standardised definitions for over 90 features with C++ core and Python interface.
rows.protocol_optimization: no: no protocol selection; applications cited include model optimisation, not test-battery design.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: reports benchmarking and usage, no held-out evaluation of a detection method.
rows.ai_transformations: no: no AI-assisted model transformation studied.

rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Component NeuroSem reuses for features; no novelty claimed there. NeuroSem adds protocol batteries, refinement-based tolerances, mutant generation, protocol selection and held-out detection evaluation on top.

rows.citation: Sáray S (2022). Systematic validation of detailed models of hippocampal neurons based on electrophysiological data. PhD thesis, Pázmány Péter Katolikus Egyetem.
rows.model_type: anatomically and biophysically detailed multicompartment NEURON (HOC) models of rat CA1 pyramidal cells and interneurons
rows.controlled_mutations: no: compares published models and successive development versions; no deliberately seeded single faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes: HippoUnit tests mimic several protocols, including somatic current injection, back-propagating AP, PSP attenuation and dendritic integration.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: feature scores (mostly Z-scores vs experimental mean/SD) averaged into per-test final scores.
rows.protocol_optimization: no: fixed expert-chosen test suite; no selection of a compact protocol set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: checks models on paradigms they were not fitted to, but no discovery/held-out split for evaluating a test method.
rows.software: HippoUnit https://github.com/KaliLab/hippounit (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API); demo models https://github.com/KaliLab/HippoUnit_demo (named in booklet, not API-checked)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Explicitly motivated by avoiding regressions across model versions, but scores agreement with experimental data. NeuroSem compares transformed to reference model, uses controlled mutants, calibrated tolerances, selected batteries and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Downloaded booklet PDF and extracted text (pypdf); REAL-PhD record page http://real-phd.mtak.hu/1773/ eprints metadata; DataCite API dois/10.15774/PPKE.ITK.2022.001 (creator, year 2022, publisher); doi.org redirect to record; GitHub API repos/KaliLab/hippounit.

rows.citation: Van Geit W, Gevaert M, Chindemi G, et al. (2016). BluePyOpt: Leveraging Open Source Software and Cloud Infrastructure to Optimise Model Parameters in Neuroscience. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 10.
rows.model_type: conductance-based neuron models (single-compartment example and detailed cell model) plus other dynamical-system use cases; parameter optimisation framework
rows.controlled_mutations: no: 'mutation' refers only to evolutionary-algorithm settings; no seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes: Protocol objects with stimuli and recordings, e.g. step current clamp; protocols can nest sub-protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes: eFEL-based features combined into multi-objective fitness scores.
rows.protocol_optimization: no: optimises model parameters for fixed protocols; does not select or minimise protocol sets.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no: paper states it does not address generalization or overfitting; only notes extra protocols could assess generalization.
rows.software: BluePyOpt https://github.com/openbraininstitute/BluePyOpt (PyPI bluepyopt 1.14.25, LGPL v3+ per PyPI license text; GitHub API NOASSERTION; BlueBrain/BluePyOpt archived)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares protocol and eFEL feature infrastructure but aims at fitting parameters to data. NeuroSem instead detects behavioural change after edits, using mutants, calibrated tolerances, protocol selection and held-out tests.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fninf.2016.00017 (authors, title, journal, vol 10, 2016-06-07); Europe PMC core record (PMID 27375471, PMC4896051) abstract and full-text XML keyword scan; GitHub API openbraininstitute/BluePyOpt and BlueBrain/BluePyOpt; PyPI JSON API bluepyopt.
